theme: Saylor teases a buy with bitcoin barely above Strategy's cost, the midterms put election-cycle charts in focus for bitcoin and stocks, SpaceX and Tesla study a merger as SpaceX's AI capex balloons, Tesla adds Fort Worth, Palantir reports tonight, and Big Tech's capex runs past its cash flow while neoclouds wait for earnings.

items.title: Strategy: bitcoin held vs its average purchase cost
items.picked: Michael Saylor posted 'We found room for even more orange' on Sunday, the tease that usually comes before a Monday purchase filing, and Strategy is one modest buy away from 850,000 BTC, per Yonhap Infomax and AInvest. Bitcoin was trading near $77,750 on Monday morning, per Fortune.
items.matters: When bitcoin trades close to Strategy's average cost, the company's paper gain on its whole stack nearly disappears, which matters for its premium and its ability to keep raising money.
items.know: On the tab's latest weekly point, Oct 30 2026, bitcoin was $77,191 against Strategy's average cost of $75,446, only about 2% above it, with 848,500 BTC held. Bitcoin was below Strategy's cost in Feb to Apr 2026 and again from Jun 5 to Aug 14 2026, when it got as low as about $60,000. The data is weekly and doesn't include any purchase filed today.

items.title: Bitcoin in midterm years: 2026 vs 2014, 2018 and 2022
items.picked: With the US midterms on Tuesday, a story trending on X has bitcoin traders arguing that past cycle lows came 71, 39 and 13 days after the 2014, 2018 and 2022 midterms, while skeptics say the 2026 low already happened in July.
items.matters: In all three midterm years in the tab bitcoin lost more than half its value, so this chart shows how far 2026 has strayed from that script.
items.know: Indexed to the prior year-end close, the tab has 2026 at 89.4 on day 305 (Nov 1), down about 11% for the year, while the midterm-year average was 44.8 on the same day. The 2014, 2018 and 2022 paths hit their lows for the year late, on days 364, 349 and 325. The 2026 low so far is 66.9 on day 181. Three past midterms is a tiny sample, and the image is the Oct 19 export, which ends around day 290.

items.title: Since the COVID low: bitcoin up, altcoins down in BTC
items.picked: A story trending on X says the altcoin market cap (the OTHERS index) just printed its first monthly bullish cross since 2023, with traders calling for altcoins to outperform in November.
items.matters: Altcoin rallies are usually measured in dollars, but priced in bitcoin most of the 2020 field has lost ground, which is the real test of whether alts beat just holding BTC.
items.know: The tab, refreshed Nov 1, has bitcoin up 1,459% in dollars since Mar 16 2020 ($5,013 to $78,135), while the median of 34 large 2020 altcoins is down 90% in BTC terms (index 10.4). Only 7 of the 34 are above their start in BTC: BNB, ZEC, DOGE, OKB, TRX, ETH and XMR. The basket drops dead coins, which flatters the result, and the image is the Oct 19 export.

items.title: SpaceX capex by segment: AI dwarfs rockets and Starlink
items.picked: SpaceX spent $19.6B on capex in Q3, $16.4B of it on its AI segment, and guided to $35-40B for Q4, per The Motley Fool. On Oct 26 it also agreed a sale-leaseback of about $40B of Nvidia hardware with an Apollo subsidiary.
items.matters: Spending at this scale is the main risk in the SpaceX story: the AI revenue only pays off if the compute it is buying keeps earning more than it costs.
items.know: For the four quarters to Sep 30 2026 the tab has $54.96B of capex: $44.65B in AI (xAI and X), $5.47B in Starlink and $4.85B in Space. For 2025 it was $20.74B, including $12.73B in AI, and in 2023 just $4.42B. The image was redrawn from the tab because the Drive export still showed the year to June.

items.title: Where Tesla Robotaxi runs
items.picked: Tesla's @robotaxi account said rides open in Fort Worth at 6am today, its fourth Texas city, per TeslaNorth. Tesla's first safety report also lists Las Vegas, Jacksonville, Phoenix and San Antonio as coming soon, per Driverless.news.
items.matters: Coverage is the simplest way to track whether robotaxi is turning into a national business or staying a few test zones.
items.know: The table lists six metros running unsupervised (Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando and Tampa), the SF Bay Area with safety drivers under a California TCP permit, and Las Vegas and Phoenix with preparations underway. It was built Oct 9 2026, so it doesn't include Fort Worth or the later launch list, and 'ramping unsupervised' is the tab's label from Tesla's Jul 22 Q2 update, not a fleet count.

items.title: Capex as a share of operating cash flow: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta
items.picked: A story trending on X says Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft spent a record $201.9B on capex in Q3 and that only Microsoft had positive free cash flow. Hedge funds also sold about $20B of US tech stocks in two weeks in October, per Goldman Sachs data cited in another trending story.
items.matters: When a company spends more than 100% of its operating cash flow on capex, it has to fund the rest from its cash pile or borrowing, which is the core of the AI spending worry.
items.know: In the Jun 2026 quarter the tab has Amazon at 119.4% and Alphabet at 115.0%, both above 100%, with Meta at 94.5% and Microsoft at 64.6%. Two years earlier, in Jun 2024, all four were at 70% or less. The tab ends with the Jun quarter, so it doesn't include the Sep-quarter results reported last week.

items.title: Neocloud valuation vs revenue run-rate
items.picked: Jim Cramer warned that anti-data-center policies after the midterms could hit neocloud stocks, per a story trending on X, after neoclouds fell when Microsoft trimmed its capex outlook. CoreWeave and Nebius report on Nov 10 and Nov 12.
items.matters: Neoclouds trade on very different multiples of their revenue, so this table shows which ones the market is paying up for ahead of earnings.
items.know: At Oct 30 closes the tab has CoreWeave at a $30.3B market cap, 2.9x its $10.3B revenue run-rate, with a $103.7B backlog, while Nebius is at $41.9B, or 18.0x. IREN is at 17.3x, and TeraWulf and Cipher are above 30x but still earn mostly from bitcoin mining. Run-rate is the latest quarter times four, and market cap is equity value, so debt isn't included.

items.title: The midterm-year pattern: the S&P 500 in 2026 vs the average midterm year
items.picked: With Tuesday's midterms ahead, a story trending on X notes the S&P 500 has risen in the 12 months after all 19 midterms since 1950. Stock futures were higher this morning after last week's tech selloff.
items.matters: Midterm years are usually weak until the election and then rally, so it helps to know where 2026 stands against that pattern.
items.know: On trading day 209 the tab has the S&P 500 at 110.7 (prior year-end = 100) versus 98.0 for the average midterm year since 1974 and 105.8 for all years since 1971. By year-end the midterm average reaches 101.9 and the all-years average 110.1. The image is the Oct 19 export, so it ends about ten trading days earlier.
